follow_ups.title: Write the design note reversing the sell-then-buy economy
follow_ups.first_action: Update the onboarding chapter's rejected-fork note and record the storage-tier numbers (on-person cap, what a silo raises it to) in the design docs and decision log
follow_ups.why: Daniel's proposal reopens a fork the docs already argued against by name; the reversal has to land in the docs before anyone builds against it.

follow_ups.title: Merge seed and crop stock so a harvest is directly plantable
follow_ups.first_action: Replace the two separate seed/crop dictionaries with one plantable/sellable stock per crop type, capped at the on-person excess threshold, and re-check the existing no-soft-lock proof against the new model since it no longer depends on a coin step
follow_ups.why: The whole first-session simplification depends on this sim change; nothing today lets a harvested crop go back in the ground.

follow_ups.title: Spec the wordless 'storage full, time to sell' signal
follow_ups.first_action: Once the excess number is fixed, extend the existing basket-pip pattern into an overflow state rather than adding a new gauge
follow_ups.why: The HUD already has the right shape (pips that stop counting past five); it just needs pointing at the new trigger.

recommend.question: Should an actual written letter ever deliver a shipment or unlock, anywhere in the game?
recommend.answer: No — every arrival stays wordless, reusing the locked-icon-lights-up and single-highlight vocabulary already shipped; nothing mechanical needs a sentence.
recommend.why: The pre-reader rule already forbids required reading in the core loop, and the studio has already solved this exact problem three times without words.
recommend.instead: If he wants a supplier's voice for flavor, put it in an optional, adult-facing log a pre-reader never has to open — never in the required path.

check.summary: Sam's reading holds up against the docs and code — days 1–2 already skip the shop, the seed-from-harvest fork is named in the onboarding chapter, and the five-pip basket exists — but the reply overstates two small things the follow-up owners should know before building.

findings.what: The basket pips Sam calls 'already in the HUD' are treatment B's draft, only drawn when that treatment is on, and the five-pip cap is tagged as a playtest guess
findings.fix: The tier-0 'storage full' item should say it is promoting a draft treatment to the shipped HUD, not repointing something live; settle the treatment before the excess number

findings.what: The onboarding chapter does not just 'turn down' seed-from-harvest — it names it as the fallback and calls it cheap to switch to, which makes the doc change a promotion of a planned fallback rather than a reversal
findings.fix: Milo's note should cite the fallback clause and record the no-soft-lock property at lines 702-704 as still required under the new model

findings.what: The recommendation claims the studio has solved wordless unlocks 'three times'; the reply itself names two mechanisms (darkened locked icon, single glow), and nothing was counted
findings.fix: Drop the number or name the third case; the claim stands fine on the two

conversation.text: I'd like to loosen the belief that everything is wordless.  Instead, the game should be generally understandable with minimal literacy.  We can show text too, but let's try every time to see how far we can get communicating without the words, since that'll always make the game more accessible to players.

decided.question: Should an actual written letter ever deliver a shipment or unlock, anywhere in the game?
decided.answer: No — every arrival stays wordless, reusing the locked-icon-lights-up and single-highlight vocabulary already shipped; nothing mechanical needs a sentence.
